Police interviews able to be used as evidence-in-chief in NSW sexual assault trials under new rules

More on today’s changes to the Criminal Procedure Act in NSW …

Under the changes, recorded police interviews will also be able to used as evidence-in-chief in sexual assault trials, requiring complainants to only provide their evidence once, including in the case of a retrial.

The NSW Women’s Safety Commissioner, Hannah Tonkin, says:

double quotation markAllowing complainants’ pre-recorded evidence in chief to be used during sexual assault trials will enable them to give their account much earlier, in a safe setting, and to start rebuilding their lives sooner.

The government is also amending the law around the handling sexual assault complainants’ counselling communications so that courts can only consider them when it is necessary, rather than automatically or out of an abundance of caution.

University of Sydney-led research, due to report back in mid-2027, is considering alternative models for reform. Recent reporting has revealed how complainants’ counselling records, including audio recordings, have been used by alleged perpetrators’ legal teams.

Minns says shooting of 11-year-old ‘very tragic reminder’ of danger of guns

The NSW premier, Chris Minns, says the shooting of an 11-year-old boy in north-west Sydney is a “very tragic reminder of how dangerous guns are”.

An 18-year-old man was charged yesterday with concealing a serious indictable offence after the incident, while two other 18-year-old men were released pending further inquiries. Speaking to ABC News Breakfast this morning, the premier said:

double quotation markIt’s obviously an incredibly distressing situation. It’s the subject of a major police investigation. I understand the adults in the house are not cooperating with police. We just urge anyone that has any information about this horrible event – we’ve got [an 11-year-old] in a serious condition in a NSW hospital – to come forward.

It’s also a very tragic reminder of how dangerous guns are, and often the people who are the victims of guns, are innocent people, many times they are children. They’re very dangerous, and we need less of them in our community.

Minns was asked about comments made by police deputy commissioner Peter McKenna after a spate of violence over the weekend, including the alleged murders of three women. McKenna said the government needed to be “throwing every resource” at domestic violence prevention. Minns said:

double quotation markWell, Peter’s an incredibly straight talker on these issues, and he’s 100% right. I mean, the number of violent crimes against often innocent people, innocent family members is hugely distressing. It’s an urgent emergency for our state and we need to throw everything we possibly can at it.

A pilot of “ground rules” hearings will reduce distress and trauma for complainants in sexual assault trials alongside other reforms being introduced to NSW parliament today, the state government says.

Ground rules hearings, which are already used in child sexual assault proceedings in NSW, will be piloted in sexual assault trials at Parramatta, Wollongong and Dubbo district courts from March next year until 2030.

They will provide directions about how complainants will be questioned, including the duration and manner, topics put to them and aides to support their evidence. The government says hearings will require pre-trial discussion about jury directions regarding consent and differences in accounts “without compromising the accused’s right to test the prosecution case”.

The NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, says:

double quotation markSexual assault complainants and witnesses are especially vulnerable in our justice system. We want to help them give their best evidence by ensuring they do not need to tell their story multiple times and deterring inappropriate and irrelevant questioning in court.

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young spoke this morning about the idea for a national authority to oversee the triple zero network, which is responsible for emergency call operations.

A Senate committee said yesterday in a report that triple zero should be taken out of private hands.

The plan would move control of Australia’s emergency call system away from commercial entities like Telstra to a dedicated public authority.

Hanson-Young told RN Breakfast this morning:

double quotation markAt the moment, Telstra is contracted to do this work. The taxpayers pay it. That’s your money, my money, every Australian taxpayer’s money to fund the operation of triple zero … We think it’s time to really consider bringing that back under independent control so that the customer, the public, the safety is put first – it’s not seen as some kind of chore or add-on for a privately run company …

There needs to be an overhaul of the telecommunications laws. Standards and reliability guarantees must be in the law. Compensation must be available for people. And triple zero must be run for the safety of people, not the profits of corporations.

title: Canada’s BC sues OpenAI over ChatGPT role in Tumbler Ridge school shooting
excerpt: The Canadian province of British Columbia has sued the California firm OpenAI for failing to notify law enforcement of threats made on its ChatGPT platform before a shooter opened fire at a school in ...
body_text:
The Canadian province of British Columbia has sued the California firm OpenAI for failing to notify law enforcement of threats made on its ChatGPT platform before a shooter opened fire at a school in Tumbler Ridge.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in San Francisco on Monday, names OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, as defendants.

The British Columbia government is seeking financial compensation from OpenAI to cover past and future costs tied to emergency response and community recovery efforts. The lawsuit also seeks a court order forcing the company to overhaul how it identifies and handles user conversations that threaten violence.

Eight victims died in the February 10, 2026 attack in the small town of Tumbler Ridge, in what officials described as one of Canada’s worst mass shootings. The shooter killed her mother and half-brother at their home before going to a secondary school, where she killed five children and an educator, and then died by suicide at the scene.

The shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, 18, a former student at the school, had been flagged by ChatGPT’s safety team after her conversations about gun violence, but the company did not alert police.

British Columbia Attorney General Niki Sharma said in a statement that Tumbler Ridge residents deserved answers and accountability.

“This action is an important step toward seeking justice for the families, students, educators and community members whose lives were forever changed,” she said.

She said the lawsuit raises serious questions about the responsibilities of tech firms when they become aware of credible threats of violence.

“This case highlights the urgent need for strong national safeguards for artificial intelligence technologies and online platforms,” she said.

Altman published a letter to the community in April, saying he was “deeply sorry” OpenAI had not contacted law enforcement. He promised reforms but never followed through, despite efforts by the province’s attorney general to engage, the lawsuit says.

The British Columbia lawsuit comes after more than 30 lawsuits were filed in the same California federal court by victims’ families, survivors and others affected by the attack, accusing OpenAI of negligence for failing to intervene and alert authorities.

title: Political fight over gun buyback after boy, 11, shot in the face and neck in Sydney apartment
excerpt:
Police don’t know if shooting was accidental as Labor attacks opposition vow to scrap gun buyback announced after Bondi massacre

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaki...
body_text:
Police don’t know if shooting was accidental as Labor attacks opposition vow to scrap gun buyback announced after Bondi massacre

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The shooting of an 11-year-old boy in Sydney’s north-west was a “tragic reminder” of the danger of guns, the New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, has said while the opposition defends “backflipping” on a gun buyback.

The child was transported to Westmead Children’s hospital in a critical condition on Monday evening after suffering gunshot wounds to his face and neck at a unit in Norwest, NSW police said.

Five other people were home at the time, including four 18-year-old men and a 44-year-old woman, none of whom were injured.

One of the men was charged with concealing a serious indictable offence, while two of the other men were arrested and released pending further inquiries.

He appeared at Blacktown local court on Tuesday morning via audiovisual link, where he made no application for bail.

Speaking to ABC TV on Tuesday, Minns said it was an “incredibly distressing situation”.

“It’s the subject of a major police investigation,” the premier said.

“I understand the adults in the house are not cooperating with police. We just urge anyone that has any information about this horrible event … to come forward.”

Minns said the incident was a “very tragic reminder” of how dangerous guns were.

“Often the people who are the victims of guns are innocent people, many times they are children,” he said. “They’re very dangerous and we need less of them in our community.”

Supt Naomi Moore said on Monday night that police had no information to suggest the shooting was related to organised crime.

“It is an absolutely tragic situation, and we’ve seen tragedy across Sydney in the last couple of days; this is not far from the worst that I’ve seen,” Moore told reporters.

She said police were investigating how the gun came to be in the house, as there were no firearms registered to the property and none of the individuals had gun licenses.

There have been at least six suspected mistaken-identity shootings in Sydney since the start of last year.

Last week, two teenage boys were charged with murder after the recent shooting death of a university student in Sydney, which police say was a case of mistaken identity.

Earlier this month, the state’s police minister denied that gang violence was out of control.

Following the Bondi beach terror attack, the state government introduced new legislation to undertake Australia’s biggest gun buyback in 30 years, with the scheme set to begin on 2 November this year.

The Liberal opposition voted with Labor in support of a buyback last year, but on Saturday pledged it would scrap Labor’s firearm ownership caps for primary producers.

The NSW opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, instead proposed a commission of inquiry into gun laws and a freeze of any buyback. Caps for farmers and professional shooters would also be scrapped.

The police minister, Yasmin Catley, called the Coalition’s plan a “stunning backflip” and said it would leave more guns in circulation.

“Our position is simple and it has not and will not change: fewer dangerous guns in circulation means a safer NSW,” Catley said.

Sloane defended the opposition’s position on Tuesday, telling ABC radio that resources should be spent on “red-flagging terrorists” and “additional policing”.

“We just think this is a government that is trying to say that they’ve made our streets safer, when this is really a very blunt instrument that’s targeting the wrong people,” she said.

title: Trump says he’ll probably lose lawsuit brought by news outlets he banned from White House, blaming judge appointed by ‘TRUMP’ – as it happened
excerpt:
US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

Donald Trump is bracing for a loss in the lawsuit brought by three media organizations, as he considers that the judge presiding ...
body_text:
US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

Donald Trump is bracing for a loss in the lawsuit brought by three media organizations, as he considers that the judge presiding over the case – his own appointee – previously ordered the White House to restore credentials for journalist Jim Acosta.

“They have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta, who now seems to have disappeared from the Planet,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, referring to a lawsuit filed by CNN in 2018. “The Judge’s name is Tim Kelly, and he was, sadly, appointed by ‘TRUMP.’ In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown ‘sources,’ shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World.”

That concludes our coverage of the second Trump administration for today. Here are the latest developments:

The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump after the administration banned journalists from several outlets from entering the White House grounds. Newsrooms including the New York Times and the Washington Post also decided to hold off on publishing or distributing still photographs taken as part of the White House pool coverage on Monday until midnight as part of the collective effort. More here.

The barred outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – sued the administration on Monday, saying the president’s actions were a violation of their first amendment rights. The parties are seeking a temporary restraining order that would immediately lift the ban – and return access for the journalists – while the case plays out. More here.

Trump is bracing for a loss in the lawsuit brought by the three media organizations, as he considers that the judge presiding over the case – his own appointee – previously ordered the White House to restore credentials for journalist Jim Acosta. “In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal,” he wrote on Truth Social.

Trump said that he hoped Zohran Mamdani would be a “great mayor” for New York, an unusually warm assessment of the democratic socialist leader whom the president and his Republican allies have spent months holding up as a symbol of the Democratic party’s alleged embrace of “communism” ahead of the November midterms. More here.

At a news conference following their closed-door meeting at Gracie Mansion, Mamdani said he and Trump held a “wide-ranging” discussion, which touched on affordable housing and immigration.

The Venezuelan man who was shot by a federal immigration officer in Texas on Sunday spoke out from detention on Monday afternoon when he was able to call his lawyer, in the middle of a press conference, and plead for better medical care. Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was taken from a hospital in Austin into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention, even though he apparently still has a bullet lodged near his spine and is in much discomfort. More here.

Lauren Boebert, the firebrand Republican subject of a House ethics complaint that she had sex with three staff members, and paid one to keep quiet, has said the allegations are untrue – and part of a “politically motivated” campaign against her. More here.

A long-running legal fight over Missouri’s congressional map took another turn Monday when a federal appeals panel ruled in favor of new districts backed by Donald Trump, even though the US supreme court has blocked those districts from being used in the November election, the AP reports.

A three-judge panel of the eighth US circuit court of appeals said Missouri should use the new Republican-drawn US House districts in the November election, just as the state did in its August primary. To revert to its prior districts for the general election would violate the US constitution, the appeals judges said.

However, the ruling has no immediate impact. That’s because the federal appellate panel delayed the effect of its order for a week to allow time for an appeal. The US supreme court already has twice sided against the Trump-backed map and had blocked enforcement of a lower court order favoring the map pending a potential appeal and eventual decision by the high court.

Missouri is currently set to run its November election with the same congressional districts it used in 2024 and 2022, following prior decisions by both the Missouri supreme court and the US supreme court.

In a press conference held on Monday, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani was in disagreement with Donald Trump’s decision to ban CNN, Politico and MS Now from the White House, and instead welcomed all members of the press at Gracie Mansion in New York.

“I told the president that we’re going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn, and that is something that I believe in – is everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique, that we engage,” Mamdani said.

US Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff are asking California attorney general Rob Bonta to look into the claims of a whistleblower alleging the Department of Homeland Security is ordering officers to impersonate voters to access online voter data.

According to the senators, officers in a unit of the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), an agency within the department, are being tasked with investigating 40 subjects per day.

The whistleblower claims that officers were instructed to pull citizens’ personal data from federal databases and enter it into the state website to gain access.

“The Trump Administration appears to be undertaking this rushed effort to find – or manufacture – evidence for its baseless election conspiracy theories of widespread voter fraud ahead of the 2026 midterm elections,” reads a letter by the senators. “Inaccurate claims of ‘unlawful voters’ and erroneous federal law enforcement records can result in serious consequences for Californians, including many naturalized citizens.”

“The Trump Administration may also use these claims to further threaten state and local election officials in California and undermine or challenge the election results themselves,” the senators added in the letter.

US Representative Ro Khanna said on Monday that the shooting of a Venezuelan man in Texas by a federal immigration officer “demands a full investigation”.

“No one should be shot in the back and denied urgent medical care,” Khanna wrote in a post on social media. “The shooting of Venezuelan DoorDash driver Wilber Garcés Pérez by ICE in Austin demands a full investigation.”

Khanna added: “Abolish ICE. Prosecute rogue agents.”

Earlier today, Garcés Pérez pleaded for better medical care. “I haven’t received any medical attention. I’m in a lot of pain,” he said.

My colleague Emiliano Tahui Gomez is reporting the latest details on the shooting:

The US is planning to reopen a former cold war-era ⁠military base in southern Greenland and set up a military presence at an east coast base, Reuters reports.

Sources told the wire that an agreement is expected to be signed by the US, Denmark and Greenland on Tuesday at the United Nations general assembly in New ‌York City.

One of these military bases, Mestersvig, ⁠is currently used by the Sirius Dog Sled Patrol. The other post is Narsarsuaq, where the population has dwindled to a few dozen people since the US closed its Bluie West One military base in the 1950s.

The agreement follows the announcement of an Arctic security pact between the US and the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, following pressure from Trump to annex the semi-autonomous Danish territory by force.

In his remarks today, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani said he shared “very strong opinions” on “how we can keep immigrant New Yorkers safe” during his meeting with Donald Trump, especially regarding temporary protected status (TPS) for immigrants in the United States.

Mamdani said he told the US president “how important immigrant New Yorkers, especially Haitian New Yorkers, are not only to the fabric of our city, but also to our city’s economy, to so many of the industries that build our city, and the stability that is in the president’s hands”.

In June, the US supreme court ruled in favor of the Trump administration’s effort to strip TPS from hundreds of thousands of Haitians and Syrians.

Zohran Mamdani was asked whether he challenged Donald Trump on the banning of CNN, MS Now, and Politico from White House grounds.

“I told the president that we’re going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn, and that is something that I believe in,” Mamdani said at Gracie Mansion in New York City.

“It’s interesting because they said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me, so I wasn’t very worried about that,” Trump said.

In response to a question about whether the ban was put in place as a distraction from the war in Iran and high gas prices, Trump said: “I’m not.”

“I’m only doing it because I think the press also has an obligation,” Trump said. “I think that these outlets have an obligation to be fair. And if they’re fake news, I really think I have an obligation not to allow them into another very special house. This is a special house, Gracie Mansion. Well, the White House is the most special of all houses.”

New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani and President Donald Trump spoke ahead of the UN General Assembly this week following a closed-door meeting at Gracie Mansion on Monday.

“One of the focuses of the conversation the president and I have been having is about the possibility of building more housing here in New York City,” Mamdani said.

“We’ve spoken about Sunnyside Yard,” he added, referring to the 180-acre railyard in Queens, “and it’s a real pleasure that just today we’ve agreed to set up a new level of that conversation between our housing and operations team at City Hall and the White House team.”

“I can tell you that Sunnyside’s a big job,” Trump said. “I’ve been watching that for 35 years. Everybody’s wanted to do something with Sunnyside Yards.”

“You’re going to need a lot of federal approvals and probably some federal money to do it. But it’s always been a great location,” Trump added.

The New York Times said it would hold off on publishing or distributing still photographs taken as part of the White House pool coverage on Monday until midnight, joining a collective effort with photographers in other newsrooms in support of the media organizations that were banned from the White House.

“The New York Times will not publish or distribute any images taken as part of the White House still photography pool today, in conjunction with the other members of that pool and in a show of support for the news organizations being unfairly targeted by the president’s barring of journalists from the White House,” said Charlie Stadtlander, a spokesperson for the news outlet, in a statement.

“We remain committed to covering the president’s travel to New York City today,” Stadtlander added. “Americans deserve a free and independent media covering their government without intimidation, as well as comprehensive coverage of newsworthy events.”

Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, the Venezuelan man who was shot by an ICE officer in Austin, spoke over the phone at a news conference, offering further details on his condition.

The 28-year-old was taken to a hospital in Austin, Texas, in serious but stable condition before being taken into custody.

The Associated Press reports that, speaking by phone during a news conference, Garcés Pérez said doctors didn’t remove the bullet because it’s near his spine.

He said ICE pressed for him to be released quickly from the hospital so officers could move him to a detention center. He said he had received no pain medication or treatment there, and had slept on the floor before eventually being given a “pill” by a nurse on Monday.

“I am not doing well due to the gunshot wound, and I have not received the medical attention that I require,” Perez said, speaking in Spanish over the phone as his wife translated during the news conference.

Donald Trump is bracing for a loss in the lawsuit brought by three media organizations, as he considers that the judge presiding over the case – his own appointee – previously ordered the White House to restore credentials for journalist Jim Acosta.

“They have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta, who now seems to have disappeared from the Planet,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, referring to a lawsuit filed by CNN in 2018. “The Judge’s name is Tim Kelly, and he was, sadly, appointed by ‘TRUMP.’ In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown ‘sources,’ shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World.”

President Donald Trump has arrived at Gracie Mansion to meet with New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, per CNN.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump called the official residence of New York City’s mayors “one of my favorite places in the World.”

“It will be interesting to see how it looks now, invited by Mayor Mamdani,” Trump wrote. “Look forward to it. MAKE NEW YORK CITY GREAT AGAIN!”

title: Trump was a 'caged lion' roaring to return to WHCA Dinner ballroom after shooting, Leavitt says
excerpt:
Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt revealed new details into President Donald Trump’s reaction to the WHCA Dinner shooting on ‘Hang Out with Sean Hannity.’

Former White House press s...
body_text:
Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt revealed new details into President Donald Trump’s reaction to the WHCA Dinner shooting on ‘Hang Out with Sean Hannity.’

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt revealed new details on President Donald Trump’s behind-the-scenes response after shots were fired at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in April.

Leavitt said in a new episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" that Trump was behaving like a caged animal and was adamant about returning to the ballroom, despite having just narrowly escaped from an alleged assassination attempt.

"He was like a caged lion backstage, like just roaring to get out, like, 'We gotta go back out there,’" she said. "And I'm sitting there like, ‘I don't know if I want to go back out there.’"

TRUMP ADMITS HE 'WASN'T MAKING IT THAT EASY' FOR SECRET SERVICE DURING WHCD SHOOTING

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt and US President Donald Trump attend the 2026 White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) Dinner at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, DC, on July 24, 2026. The 2026 WHCA Dinner was originally scheduled for April 25 at the Washington Hilton, but was rescheduled and relocated after an alleged gunman breached security. (Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images)

Minutes after the WHCA Dinner began at the Washington Hilton, a gunman, later identified as Cole Allen of Torrance, Calif., allegedly stormed the hotel while armed with weapons. Trump and Vice President JD Vance were quickly escorted out of the ballroom by members of the Secret Service.

Allen, who was quickly apprehended by Secret Service agents, allegedly wrote in a manifesto that his targets were Trump administration officials except for FBI Director Kash Patel.

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER SHOOTING: TIMELINE TRACES HOW SUSPECT’S ALLEGED CROSS-COUNTRY PLAN UNFOLDED

Guests dived under tables as the gala, meant to celebrate White House correspondents, descended into chaos.

Yet, Leavitt said, the president was eager to return to the ballroom and willing to wait hours for the event to resume.

Armed Secret Service agents stand on stage during a shooting incident at the annual White House Correspondents' Association Dinner at the Washington Hilton on April 25, 2026, in Washington, D.C. According to reports, President Donald Trump and other government officials were evacuated from the venue after gunshots. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"[Trump] really was asking hard questions of his detail, like, ‘Why can't I go? I will wait all night. I don't care if it's 3 in the morning, get it started,’" Leavitt shared.

The former White House spokeswoman said officials even began making preparations to resume the dinner as she described Trump’s impatience to make a public statement immediately after the incident.

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER SHOOTING SHARPENS FOCUS ON TRUMP’S BALLROOM CONSTRUCTION PROPOSAL

"[Trump] wanted to say something and the best way to say it was in the briefing room. And we did," Leavitt said.

Trump held a news conference at the White House later that night alongside top administration members, recounting how the shooting unfolded.

US President Donald Trump holds a press conference at the White House in Washington, DC, shortly after a shooting incident at the White House Correspondents' Dinner on April 25, 2026. (Celal Gunes/Anadolu via Getty Images)

After the shooting, the president reignited calls to build a ballroom at the White House to create a space for safe and secure official events. Trump attended the rescheduled WHCA Dinner that took place in July.

Leavitt’s full interview on the latest "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" will be available Tuesday on YouTube, Spotify and Apple.

Nora Moriarty is a Writer at Fox News Digital.

title: Sylvester Stallone reveals what he said to Trump after surprise Hollywood ambassador appointment
excerpt:
Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo brings ‘The Ingraham Angle’ to the red carpet at the Kennedy Center Honors and interviews stars in music and Hollywood.

Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was bli...
body_text:
Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo brings ‘The Ingraham Angle’ to the red carpet at the Kennedy Center Honors and interviews stars in music and Hollywood.

Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced his appointment as a special ambassador to Hollywood.

Days before his second inauguration in January 2025, Trump shared a post on his platform Truth Social in which he named Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as "Special Envoys," describing the role as a way for the three actors to serve as his "eyes and ears" in Hollywood and advise him on efforts to bring film and television production back to the U.S.

During a recent interview with The Sunday Times, the 80-year-old "Rocky" star recalled that he found out about the appointment while watching television.

SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!'

"I was watching TV one night, and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, ‘This is not possible,'" Stallone said.

Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced him as a "special Hollywood ambassador." (Weiss Eubanks/NBCUniversal via Getty Images; Artur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Stallone told the outlet that he was hesitant about taking on the role because he didn't believe it was feasible. When asked if he had reservations after Trump's announcement, Stallone said, "Yes. Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states."

'AMERICAN IDOL' DITCHES HOLLYWOOD FOR GEORGIA AFTER TWO DECADES AS CALIFORNIA LOSES ANOTHER PRODUCTION

"They have their little kingdoms," he continued. "You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people. No, it won’t work."

The "Tulsa King" star recalled that he later explained his reasoning to Trump.

"I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible," Stallone said. "Hollywood works, and it will evolve."

"It’s corporate, and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance," he added.

Stallone said he told Trump that the role was "not possible." (Joe Raedle)

'I PLAY ROCKY' REVIVES THE GAMBLE THAT MADE SYLVESTER STALLONE A SUPERSTAR

In his original post on Jan. 16, 2025, Trump wrote, "It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California."

"They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!" he continued. "These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!"

DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON REJECTS HOLLYWOOD’S POLITICAL OBSESSION, BLASTS CELEBRITY ATTACK CULTURE

At the time, Gibson, 70, shared that he was caught off-guard by Trump's announcement and did not have previous knowledge about his presidential appointment.

Gibson said he was "surprised" by Trump's announcement.  (Mike Marsland/Mike Marsland/WireImage via Getty Images)

"I got the tweet at the same time as all of you and was just as surprised," he told Variety in January 2025. "Nevertheless, I heed the call. My duty as a citizen is to give any help and insight I can."

"Any chance the position comes with an Ambassador’s residence?" Gibson joked.

Though Stallone may not have been onboard with his role as a special Hollywood ambassador, the action star appears to have a friendly relationship with Trump and heaped praise on the president during a speech following his victory in the November 2024 election.

Days after the election, Stallone introduced Trump at the America First Policy Institute Gala held at the president-elect's Mar-A-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida.

"We’re in the presence of a really mythical character," Stallone said of Trump. "I love mythology. And this individual does not exist on this planet. Nobody in the world could have pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe."

"When George Washington defended his country, he had no idea that he was gonna change the world," he added. "Because without him, you could imagine what the world would look like. Guess what? We got the second George Washington."

Stallone was later selected as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree, with Trump personally naming him among that year’s recipients alongside George Strait, KISS, Gloria Gaynor and Michael Crawford.

Trump named Stallone as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree. (Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images)

The actor has backed Republicans, including John McCain and Trump, but his political history has not been strictly partisan. Over the years, Stallone has made financial contributions to both political parties, donating to various Democratic candidates and committees, including former President Joe Biden and the Democratic National Committee, as well as Republican campaigns.

Meanwhile, Voight, who is a staunch supporter of Trump, appears to have embraced his role as a special ambassador. He has met with the White House and advocated for policies aimed at bringing film and TV production back to the U.S., especially a federal film tax incentive. Voight has been working with his manager Steven Paul and Paul’s associate Scott Karol as part of his push.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

After meeting with the trio at the end of last month, Trump threw his support behind a federal film and television production incentive, urging Congress to pass bipartisan legislation to "save" the American entertainment business.

In a Truth Social post on Aug. 31, Trump wrote that "Hollywood is a Complete and Total Disaster" and said there was "no incentive" for productions to stay there. He said meetings were being set up with leaders of both parties and urged Republicans and Democrats to "immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America."

Trump has a longtime friend in Voight, who he also appointed as a special ambassador to Hollywood.  (Mandel Ngan)

Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (D-CA) later issued statements in which they voiced their support for Trump's proposal.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

While speaking with the Hollywood Reporter earlier this month, Voight was asked whether Stallone and Gibson were involved with his efforts.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

They’ve been very busy, both of those guys actually have been extremely busy," Voight said.

However, Paul, who joined Voight for the interview, said, "Sly’s been doing his TV show, but Sly’s been very involved and he signed our letter."

Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

title: Former cop Beau Lamarre-Condon argues self-defence in double murder trial citing struggle over gun
excerpt:
Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to fatally shooting Jesse Baird, 26, and his partner, 29-year-old Luke Davies, with police service weapon in 2024

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest ...
body_text:
Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to fatally shooting Jesse Baird, 26, and his partner, 29-year-old Luke Davies, with police service weapon in 2024

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former police officer claims he killed two men in self-defence and began cleaning up the crime scene because he “panicked”, a Sydney court has heard.

Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting 26-year-old Jesse Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, 29, with a police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.

The prosecution told the supreme court on Monday that Lamarre-Condon had become infatuated and obsessed with Baird and began planning his murder in early 2024.

Lamarre-Condon’s defence lawyer, John Stratton SC, told the court on Tuesday that the policeman had been acting in “self-defence”.

Disguised as an Uber Eats driver, Lamarre-Condon had entered the home in a motorcycle helmet, so he would not be recognised while picking up his belongings, Stratton said. He had a key he was given by Baird, the jury was told.

But because Baird did not recognise Lamarre-Condon, a struggle ensued during which the 26-year-old was killed, the defence barrister told the jury.

The officer’s gun was then flung across the room and Davies picked it up, Stratton told the court. Lamarre-Condon then grabbed Davies by the arm and pushed the gun towards him.

In the struggle that followed, Davies pulled the trigger and shot himself, the court was told.

“It’s his case that what he did was self-defence,” Stratton said. “[He was] understandably panicked. He was a police officer and he knew this looked bad.”

Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.

Earlier on Tuesday, crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC outlined how Lamarre-Condon allegedly murdered the two men and concealed their bodies, as the trial entered its second day.

The prosecution alleged Lamarre-Condon entered Baird’s house with a stolen key before shooting him twice and shooting Davies through a bedroom door.

Audio of the three shots was played to the courtroom: the first two coming in quick succession before the third, 51 seconds later. Baird and Davies’ loved ones wiped away tears as they listened in court.

The crown alleges that after the murders, Lamarre-Condon immediately began to clean up the crime scene and moved the bodies. He told a friend he had killed two people, the court heard.

According to Hatfield, when the friend asked if he was joking, Lamarre-Condon responded: “I wish I was, I don’t feel like it was me … I feel like I need some help, this job has fucked me up.”

Asked how he did it, Lamarre-Condon allegedly said “with a gun” and made a hand gesture and said “pew pew”.

The friend refused to help and Lamarre-Condon later bought a second surfboard bag – days after he had bought the first, the jury was told.

He returned to Baird’s home that afternoon before one of Baird’s housemates came home.

“She did notice the two surfboard bags which, at this stage, were in the back courtyard,” Hatfield told the court.

“She will tell you what she thought was rust [was] seeping out from the bags. She took a photo and sent it to her housemate but didn’t realise at the time that the bags contained two bodies.”

A photo of outdoor furniture with a pool of blood was shown to the court on Tuesday.

Lamarre-Condon would eventually buy a bag of quick set concrete and weights, and take the bags to a dam near Goulburn, the crown prosecutor said.

Lamarre-Condon mixed the concrete and put it into the bags with the weights in an unsuccessful attempt to make the bodies sink, Hatfield said.

He later moved the bodies to a fence line near a monastery in Bungonia where they were found eight days later, the jury was told.

On Monday, Hatfield said Lamarre-Condon had developed an “infatuation and obsession” with Baird which manifested in compulsive behaviour that escalated after Baird ended their brief relationship.

The trial before justice Natalie Adams continues.

title: Mamdani tells Trump banned White House outlets are welcome at NYC meeting
excerpt:
President Trump defends his decision to ban certain news outlets from the White House as Mamdani addresses inviting all media to Gracie Mansion.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday said NYC ...
body_text:
President Trump defends his decision to ban certain news outlets from the White House as Mamdani addresses inviting all media to Gracie Mansion.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday said NYC welcomed all members of the media for a joint meeting with President Donald Trump, who recently banned certain media outlets from the White House.

The remarks came during a press conference at Gracie Mansion, where a reporter asked Mamdani whether he had challenged Trump on his decision to bar CNN, MS NOW, and Politico.

"I told the president that we're going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn. And that is something that I believe in, as everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique that we engage in," Mamdani said.

Trump then took the stage, defending his decision and addressing the subsequent suspension of presidential pool coverage by the remaining television networks, which included FOX News Media, ABC News, CBS News, CNN and NBC News.

TRUMP, MAMDANI SET TO MEET AGAIN ON MAYOR’S HOME TURF AFTER MONTHS OF POLITICAL WHIPLASH

President Donald Trump meets with NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani inside Gracie Mansion on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. (Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani @NYCMayor)

"It's interesting because they said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me. So I wasn't very worried about that. Look at all that press," Trump said.

He then explained why he chose to engage with the outlets at Gracie Mansion despite what he described as their failure to fairly cover his accomplishments, including winning the election, settling wars and improving economic numbers.

"I'm only doing it because I think the press also has an obligation," he said.

"We have the best economic numbers for the country in the history of our country. We have $21 trillion pouring in, the biggest number ever... Nobody's ever done what we've done," he added.

WHITE HOUSE WON'T BACK DOWN AS ATTORNEY PREDICTS HOW TRUMP'S LATEST PRESS TUSSLE WILL PLAY OUT IN COURT

Trump then argued that allowing certain media outlets into the White House would be harmful to national security, accusing them of reporting what he called "fake news."

"I never get anything positive. It's always negative, even having to do with the war. We've done so well," he said, referring to Iran.

"You would think that an outlet would write at least reasonably well, but never. If you look at CNN, it’s fake news," he added.

FILE — White House television pool members FOX News Media, ABC News, CBS News, CNN and NBC News announced Monday they have agreed to suspend their pooled coverage of President Donald Trump. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)

"They're very bad for the country, very bad for national security. So I have that obligation. So we'll see how it works out," he said.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban
excerpt:
White House promoted its own ‘Trump TV’ feed online after ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC decline to participate

The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump...
body_text:
White House promoted its own ‘Trump TV’ feed online after ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC decline to participate

The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump after the administration banned journalists from several outlets from entering the White House grounds.

The collective decision came after the barred outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – sued the administration on Monday, saying the president’s actions were a violation of their first amendment rights.

The ban was an extraordinary escalation of Trump’s battle against news outlets. After a coalition of networks including ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC – which along with CNN form a press “pool” that share the responsibilities of capturing and distributing footage of the president carried by news outlets worldwide – announced they would cease coverage in solidarity with the barred outlets, the White House promoted its own feed online, branding it “Trump TV”. The channel purported to show “top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place”.

“Get real-time updates and live events streamed DIRECTLY to your phone,” the White House posted on social media. “No noise. Just the news that matters most – straight from the Trump Administration.”

It is extremely rare for a president to travel or make public appearances without the accompaniment of a representative from the White House television pool. Network cameras have provided coverage of the president since 1950.

On Monday, the ban against CNN meant that no broadcaster was covering Trump’s midday ribbon-cutting to unveil a new White House helipad. Although the White House provided a livestream, without professional boom mics and audio setup, the president’s remarks were inaudible over the sounds of a helicopter’s engine running in the background.

The president abruptly announced his ban against outlets this weekend in a Truth Social post, saying he had enough of “purposely negative stories” about him. Journalists had their press badges confiscated by Secret Service on Saturday.

“Effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage of the President,” Bryan Boughton, Fox News’s Washington bureau chief who is also currently serving on as TV pool chair, wrote in an email to pool members Monday. The role is rotated each quarter. “This follows the White House’s position preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties,” said Boughton.

In a show of support with the banned outlets, several outlets, including the Washington Post, the New York Times and the Associated Press, said they would not publish or distribute images taken as part of the White House photography pool including Trump’s departure on Marine One and his events at the United Nations in New York, until midnight ET. In a statement, the Washington Post described the action as part of a “collective effort”.

The five news networks, including CNN, wrote in a joint statement: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”

Although the broadcast networks said they would withhold televised coverage, the print, radio and wire service press pool continues to provide reports detailing Trump’s movements throughout the day.

Hours after the broadcast networks’ announcement, the Washington Post said it would also withhold its photographs of presidential events from being published until after midnight ET to support banned outlets.

On Friday, Trump abruptly announced he was banning CNN, Politico and MS Now from the White House because, he believes, they “constantly write or report FICTION and LIES”. On Saturday, reporters and other staff from the news organizations were denied access to the White House.

Other media outlets and first amendment advocacy groups responded by condemning Trump’s ban, calling it an infringement on the right to a free press.

On Monday, CNN, Politico and MS Now filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration, asking a federal judge to temporarily block the enforcement of the ban and restore the reporters’ passes to the White House.

On Truth Social, Trump defended his decisions, insisting that his ban was not “instituting an assault on the Free Press”, but instead addressing “national security” threats – a claim the US president has recently used to justify building a triumphal arch and the White House ballroom.

title: Trump and Mamdani appear friendly after ‘wide-ranging’ meeting at Gracie Mansion
excerpt:
Republican president said he hoped the democratic socialist would be a ‘great mayor’ for New York City

Donald Trump said on Monday that he hoped Zohran Mamdani would be a “great mayor” for New York, ...
body_text:
Republican president said he hoped the democratic socialist would be a ‘great mayor’ for New York City

Donald Trump said on Monday that he hoped Zohran Mamdani would be a “great mayor” for New York, an unusually warm assessment of the democratic socialist leader whom the president and his Republican allies have spent months holding up as a symbol of the Democratic party’s alleged embrace of “communism” ahead of the November midterms.

At a news conference following their closed-door meeting at Gracie Mansion, Trump and Mamdani appeared friendly as they have in previous meetings. Mamdani said he and Trump held a “wide-ranging” discussion, which touched on affordable housing and immigration, but did not offer extensive details regarding any disagreements between them.

Asked whether he challenged Trump over his decision to ban CNN, MS Now, and Politico from White House grounds, Mamdani said: “I told the president that we’re going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn, and that is something that I believe in.”

“It’s interesting because they said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me, so I wasn’t very worried about that,” Trump chimed in, pointing to the large assembly of press on the lawn.

The visit to Gracie Mansion, ahead of the president’s speech to the United Nations general assembly on Tuesday, was a measure of Trump’s apparent respect for the 34-year-old mayor of his native New York. It was the first presidential visit to the historic riverside residence in 45 years, following Ronald Reagan, who met there with Ed Koch in 1981.

Pressed on why he had invited Trump, Mamdani said he was willing to work with anybody who could “deliver” for New Yorkers, and highlighted their shared interest in building thousands of new housing units at Sunnyside Yard in Queens. For his part, Trump said he believed Mamdani had “great potential”.
 It was the latest unlikely meeting between Trump, a rightwing populist who has targeted immigrants and Muslims, and Mamdani, a democratic socialist who was born in Uganda and is New York’s first Muslim mayor.
 Trump has focused his midterm election campaign on denouncing Democrats as “godless communists” who seek to abolish borders and prisons and pose the greatest threat that the US has ever faced.
 Yet on Monday he said of Mamdani, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America: “I certainly hope he will be a great mayor. You have to understand – I want what’s good for New York. I want what’s good for the country ... I want him to be a great mayor.”
 The body language again seemed amicable. Trump deferentially stood aside as Mamdani spoke from the lectern and, when the press conference finished, gave him an affectionate double tap on the arm.
 Trump, Mamdani, Trump’s chief of staff Susie Wiles and Mamdani’s chief of staff Elle Bisgaard-Church were all in attendance during Monday’s meeting.
 Mamdani said that they discussed the Trump administration’s stripping of protections for Haitian immigrants.
 “I shared my very strong opinions about how we can keep New Yorkers safe, how we can keep immigrant New Yorker safe, and how important immigrant New Yorkers, especially Haitian New Yorkers, are – not only to the fabric of our city, but also to our city’s economy,” Mamdani said.
 “The president and I have been very frank about the many disagreements we have,” he added.

The meeting came one day after Mamdani, and Clara Brugada, the mayor of Mexico City, met with migrant delivery workers in New York City, who expressed precarity and fear surrounding the increase in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrests.
 Earlier this month, Mamdani helped initiate a lawsuit against the Trump administration for its “public charge” rule change targeting immigrant communities. The lawsuit was filed by the State of New York and 21 other states against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and various of its agencies. It is unclear if they discussed the lawsuit during the meeting.

title: Maryland hunter's alleged mistake leaves Delaware mother dead
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Maryland hunter is accused of fatally shooting a woman after mistaking her for a deer while she walked through a Del...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Maryland hunter is accused of fatally shooting a woman after mistaking her for a deer while she walked through a Delaware field with her children, according to state police.

Walter Moorhead, 74, was arrested for manslaughter and other charges after he shot Santos Maria Chilel Soto, 39, on Friday evening in Ellendale, Delaware, State Police said in a press release.

Soto was walking through an open field with a man and two children at around 7:40 p.m. as Moorhead was hunting deer from a ground blind, which is a camouflaged structure used by hunters to hide from the sight of game animals.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA AFTER ARMED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY POINTS GUN AT PEOPLE, SHOOTS AT OFFICERS

Walter Moorhead, 74, was arrested for manslaughter and other charges. (Delaware State Police)

According to police, Moorhead believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle, striking Soto.

State troopers responded to the scene and provided life-saving medical care before Soto was rushed to a local hospital, where she was later pronounced dead.

Moorhead was was slapped with multiple felony charges — manslaughter recklessly causing the death of another person, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony and three counts of first-degree reckless endangerment.

SUSPECT IN DEATHS OF 5 FOUND DEAD AFTER COPS UNCOVER GRIM SCENE AT RURAL PROPERTY OUTSIDE PORTLAND

Santos Maria Chilel Soto was described as a mother of five children and a "beloved" aunt. (Iglesia De Dios Fuente De Verdad Delaware)

He was released from custody after posting a $43,000 cash bond.

The incident remains under investigation.

Soto was described as a mother of five children and a "beloved" aunt, according to a GoFundMe page.

"Maria’s family is now facing the overwhelming pain of this sudden loss while also trying to make sure she is laid to rest with dignity," the fundraiser reads. "This heartbreaking situation has placed a heavy financial burden on the family at a time when they are grieving deeply."

Police said Walter Moorhead mistakenly believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The fundraiser was launched to help the family cover funeral services and the cost of sending her body to Guatemala. Roughly $12,000 has been raised as of Monday evening.

title: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffers knee injury against Rams, possible MCL issue feared
excerpt: Danny Parkins lists the Coolest Stats entering Week 2 of the 2026/27 NFL season, including Jaxson Dart being primed for a great performance vs. the Los Angeles Rams, and the questions surrounding the ...
body_text:
Danny Parkins lists the Coolest Stats entering Week 2 of the 2026/27 NFL season, including Jaxson Dart being primed for a great performance vs. the Los Angeles Rams, and the questions surrounding the defenses of the Denver Broncos and Houston Texans. Plus Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes preview the matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions.

The optimism and good tidings the New York Giants enjoyed through the first week of the NFL season are suddenly on hold as the team is busy evaluating the status of injured quarterback Jaxson Dart.

Dart, in his second NFL season, injured his left knee during the first series of the Monday Night Football game between the Giants and Los Angeles Rams.

The injury happened on a first-quarter hit when Dart was hit by Rams defenders both high and low. And the low hit seemed to cause his left knee to bend in a manner it is not meant to bend.

That's not all. The team also had a bit of a scare when receiver Malik Nabers left the game after a pass thrown his way fell incomplete. He was seen clutching his right shoulder.

Jaxson Dart No. 6 of the New York Giants walks off the field after a play against the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., on Sept. 21, 2026. (Getty Images)

JOHN HARBAUGH AND JAXSON DART AIM TO PULL THE NEW YORK GIANTS OUT OF THE NFC EAST BASEMENT

Both players are officially questionable to return, but it is unlikely Dart will return at all.

Nabers did indeed return after missing a series nursing his shoulder on the bench.

The hit on Dart left the quarterback on the ground clutching at the knee of his forward leg when he throws. That is never a good sign.

The saving grace: Dart's leg was not planted on the turf when he was hit.

PATRICK MAHOMES ANSWERS TROUBLING QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS SERIOUS KNEE INJURY ON FIRST DRIVE OF THE CHIEFS SEASON

That allowed the entire part of the lower leg to bend with the knee.

So the chances of this being a season-ending ACL tear are not exceedingly high.

MALIK NABERS REVEALS HOW GIANTS COACH JOHN HARBAUGH HELPED HIM OVERCOME HIS ACL INJURY FEARS

But there seems to be a possibility Dart suffered some sort of MCL issue, according to an NFL source. If that is confirmed, Dart won't need surgery, but will miss some time.

Dart limped off the field and was initially treated in the team's medical tent. Several teammates huddled outside the medical tent while Dart was inside, no doubt worried about the status of their starting quarterback.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Dart was eventually escorted to the locker room, limping there under his own power.

Backup quarterback Jameis Winston came on in his absence.

title: Footballers and fans pay tribute to Noah Woods after toddler’s death in Suffolk
excerpt:
Players in Everton v Ipswich Town match wear black armbands as supporters join in minute’s applause

Players wore black armbands during Everton’s home match against Ipswich Town on Saturday, as part o...
body_text:
Players in Everton v Ipswich Town match wear black armbands as supporters join in minute’s applause

Players wore black armbands during Everton’s home match against Ipswich Town on Saturday, as part of a tribute to three-year-old Noah Woods, whose body was found after he went missing in Suffolk this week.

A photograph of the boy was shown on the big screen before the Premier League game in Liverpool and three minutes after kick-off both sets of supporters stood to applaud in memory of Noah.

The toddler, who was non-verbal, partially deaf and had been undergoing an assessment for autism, became separated from a relative after visiting a playground in Brantham on Tuesday afternoon, Suffolk police said.

About 1,300 members of the public joined a search which ended on Wednesday when police divers recovered a body from a nearby lake.

On Thursday, Noah’s father Rhys Woods paid tribute to his son in a message shared on a community Facebook group.

He wrote: “There are no words to describe the pain of this loss, we are all absolutely heartbroken, Noah was the sweetest and most innocent little boy, with nothing but love to give, and we are going to miss him so very much.”

Ipswich Town’s captain Dara O’Shea and goalkeeper Christian Walton were among a delegation from the Suffolk club who laid flowers at the playground where he went missing.

Town defender Leif Davis donated £2,000 to a fundraising appeal set up by Good Dads Club, a group of fathers in Colchester, Essex, to support Noah’s family. It had already received more than £100,000 in donations from more than 6,000 supporters by Saturday evening.

Suffolk constabulary said the child’s death was not being treated as suspicious but that the force still has a number of inquiries to complete before submitting a file to the coroner.

title: Flight attendants reveal 90-second 'hotel room autopsy' that could save your life
excerpt:
Lynn Elmhirst, host and producer of "World’s Greatest Cruises," discusses a passenger’s medical evacuation during an Alaska voyage.

Before unpacking their bags, many flight attendants perform what th...
body_text:
Lynn Elmhirst, host and producer of "World’s Greatest Cruises," discusses a passenger’s medical evacuation during an Alaska voyage.

Before unpacking their bags, many flight attendants perform what they call a "hotel room autopsy" — a quick, six-step safety check to make sure their room is safe before settling in.

The routine is popular among airline crew members who spend hundreds of nights in hotels each year, and it includes everything from checking door locks to locating emergency exits.

"This is not a nervous habit," a recent post from CabinCrew24, an online resource for flight attendants and aviation professionals, said. "It comes from years of sleeping in strange rooms, in different countries, under different fire rules and different levels of hotel security."

'DO NOT PHYSICALLY RESIST': US ISSUES CHILLING ROBBERY WARNING FOR AMERICANS OVERSEAS

Some of the advice even aligns with recommendations from the U.S. State Department for hotel safety, Travel + Leisure reported.

Flight attendants say spending about 90 seconds checking a hotel room before unpacking can help travelers become familiar with their surroundings and identify potential safety concerns. (iStock)

First, flight attendants scan the room to make sure nobody is inside. They keep the door propped open to check and also make sure that housekeeping has finished cleaning.

"I just want to familiarize myself with the space and make sure everything looks as it should," Aura Martinez, a New York-based flight attendant for 19 years, told Fox News Digital. "It doesn't need to become a 20-minute inspection."

AIRBNB GUESTS CHECK INTO THEIR RENTAL TO FIND STARTLING DISCOVERY ON WALL

Then, they inspect common hiding spots including the bathroom, shower, bathtub, closets and behind the curtains.

Experts say travelers should briefly inspect common hiding spots, including closets, bathrooms and behind curtains, when checking into a hotel room. (iStock)

Next, frequent travelers locate the nearest emergency exit. They also review the evacuation map posted on the back of the hotel room door in case of a fire or other emergency.

"In an actual emergency, that's not when you want to be figuring out the floor plan for the first time," Brian Rooney, Texas-based travel advisor and founder of GetCruiseInfo.com, told Fox News Digital.

VACATION PARADISE UNDER ATTACK AS OFFICIALS SUSPECT ARSONISTS MAY BE BEHIND INFERNO

Martinez recommends taking it a step further.

Before unpacking, some frequent travelers recommend inspecting a hotel's locks, exits and other safety features. (iStock)

"Know whether you turn left or right when you leave your room, approximately how far the stairwell is and, if possible, how many doors you would pass before reaching it," she said.

Flight attendants also check the locks to make sure the doors, deadbolt, security latch and windows lock properly.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

They also advise making sure the room phone is working so that they can reach the front desk or emergency services in case their cellphone isn't working.

"If someone unexpectedly comes to the door claiming to be hotel staff, call the front desk and verify before opening it," Rooney added.

Experts recommend using caution when someone unexpectedly knocks, even if they claim to be hotel staff. (iStock)

Martinez agreed, adding, "You can be courteous and still be cautious."

Finally, experts recommend placing a portable door alarm or door wedge at the base of the door so you know if someone is trying to enter.

"A portable door alarm or wedge can provide an additional layer of reassurance, particularly for a solo traveler, but it shouldn't replace checking that the hotel's own locks work correctly," Rooney said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Martinez also said a small flashlight is an "incredibly underrated" item to pack for your travels.

Experts say hotel safety is about being prepared, not fearful. (iStock)

The goal is to be aware of your surroundings — not to be scared out of traveling, Rooney added. "A minute or two spent checking the room, the lock and the emergency exit lets you get on with enjoying the trip."

Martinez agreed, saying, "The purpose is to be prepared, not frightened."

Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

title: New Jersey mom charged with obstruction after 'missing' son found hiding in her crawl space
excerpt: Three New Jersey teenagers who vanished from a train station on Friday were found safe in Connecticut. Authorities used K9s and drones in an extensive search, but the motive behind their actions remai...
body_text:
Three New Jersey teenagers who vanished from a train station on Friday were found safe in Connecticut. Authorities used K9s and drones in an extensive search, but the motive behind their actions remains unclear.

A New Jersey woman was charged with obstruction this week after her missing son was found hiding in a crawl space in her home, authorities confirmed.

After the 17-year-old boy’s father reported that his son wasn’t at his scheduled drop-off on Tuesday evening, his mother, Jennifer Buckley, reportedly told police the boy wasn’t at her house and she couldn’t find him.

She also reportedly said that the boy didn’t want to go to his father’s home and expressed concern that he might be a danger to himself.

MISSING TEEN FOUND HIDING IN CONVICTED SEX OFFENDER'S CLOSET IN FLORIDA, SHERIFF SAYS

An East Brunswick police vehicle is seen. (East Brunswick Police Department)

"The East Brunswick Police Department initiated an extensive effort to locate the juvenile," the department said. "Patrol officers and other department personnel devoted significant resources to the search, while detectives conducted a follow-up investigation in the days that followed."

The investigation, which included putting the teen’s information into the National Crime Information Center, uncovered a number of discrepancies in Buckley’s story.

FLORIDA-LED OPERATION RESCUES 163 CHILDREN AROUND GLOBE IN HISTORIC STATE SWEEP, HUNTS SUSPECTED PREDATORS

When police finally did a search of her home, the boy was found hiding in a crawl space in the basement, and officers determined he had been there the whole time and she helped conceal him.

There is no evidence he was harmed in any way.

The boy was found hiding in a crawl space in his mom's basement. File photo. (Victor J. Blue/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

BABYSITTER ACCUSED OF KIDNAPPING TWO YOUNG SISTERS WAS PREVIOUSLY CHARGED WITH ABDUCTING NEWBORN

She was arrested and charged with obstructing the administration of law.

Jennifer Buckley was arrested and charged with obstruction. (Mykola Tys/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

"Whenever a juvenile is reported missing, particularly when there are concerns for that child's safety, our officers take the report seriously and commit the resources necessary to locate them," East Brunswick Police Chief Frank LoSacco said in a statement. "I commend the patrol officers, detectives, and other personnel who worked diligently to locate this juvenile and ensure his safety. Providing false or misleading information to law enforcement undermines those efforts and unnecessarily diverts officers and resources away from members of our community who may need immediate police assistance."

Fox News Digital has reached out to the East Brunswick Police Department for more information.

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Saudi-led coalition says defences intercept Houthi missile fired at Riyadh
excerpt:
Saudi-led coalition forces fighting Yemen’s Houthis have said that the Iran-backed group fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh at dawn before it was intercepted and destroyed.

“The Houthis also attempt...
body_text:
Saudi-led coalition forces fighting Yemen’s Houthis have said that the Iran-backed group fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh at dawn before it was intercepted and destroyed.

“The Houthis also attempted to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu,” coalition forces spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki wrote on X on Saturday, adding that the attacks were thwarted by the Gulf monarchy’s air defences.

Saudi Arabia warned of a “hostile aerial threat” and issued a string of emergency alerts across the kingdom overnight on Friday.

On Saturday, at least one explosion was heard in Riyadh, with residents near the airport saying they saw a large plume of black smoke later in the morning. Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage.

It was the first air raid alert sounded in Riyadh since an escalation in fighting with the Houthis in Yemen began in July.

The Saudi spokesman said that the Houthis are escalating their attempts to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in the capital. He also affirmed the coalition command’s right to take “appropriate” action to deter the Houthis, in accordance with international humanitarian law.

Earlier on Saturday, Houthi fighters in Yemen said they attacked “sensitive” sites in Riyadh as well as an Aramco oil facility in the western coastal city of Yanbu, according to a statement shared by Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree.

Saree said the Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia with cruise and ballistic missiles as well as drones.

“You could see that the Houthis are determining the timelines and the levels of the escalation,” Yasmeen al-Eryani, executive director for knowledge production at the Sana’a Center think tank, told Al Jazeera. “So, depending on the current situation, it seems that the Houthis are the ones in control,” she added.

Meanwhile, on the ground in Yemen, the armed forces of the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government said their fighters thwarted a Houthi infiltration attempt in the al-Fuliahan sector in southern Marib on Saturday, killing 12 Houthi fighters and injuring others.

The army also said 13 Yemeni soldiers were killed in two days of clashes with Houthi forces in the southwestern provinces of Taiz and Lahj.

Renewed clashes are taking place in Yemen’s Marib, Taiz, Lahj, al-Jawf and al-Bayda as part of a military escalation that began in early July – the most intense since the relative calm following an April 2022 truce.

Al-Eryani told Al Jazeera that military options against the Houthis are currently limited because much of the fighting is taking place in mountainous terrain that is difficult for opposing forces to access and hold.

For now, she said, containing the group may be a more realistic option than defeating it militarily. “Without controlling the peaks that are parallel to the coast, you will not be able to control the coast,” said al-Eryani.
